paragraph: The [Council of Ministers communique of 14 October 2026](<https://primature.gov.bi/communique-de-presse-n-13-2026-de-la-reunion-du-conseil-des-ministres-du-14-octobre-2026-le-numerique-la-securite-alimentaire-lenergie-et-la-transformation-agricole-au-coeur-du-conse/>) records the adoption of the National Digital Policy. In the last twelve months the Council adopted the policy. In 2020 the [World Bank's assessment](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/605991608528899689/pdf/Burundi-Digital-Economy-Assessment.pdf>) had found no overarching and cohesive digital strategy. The communique names no body to deliver the policy and no budget line. No text, period, delivery plan or reporting has been found for it. The nearest instrument with a period is the [ICT policy PNDTIC, which ran from 2010 to 2025](<https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/094ae7e492b4b741f58747465021caf0-0200022021/original/DE4A-Burundi-EN.pdf>). Establishing would need an adopted strategy with a public text and a period that has not ended.

The Ministry of Digital and Digitalisation ran the [5-6 February 2026 seminar that drafted the vision for the Stratégie numérique du Bénin 2031](<https://beninwebtv.bj/en/digital-benin-outlines-its-strategic-vision-for-2031>), with Deloitte. On 24 March 2026 [ASIN's director general said the agency was supporting the digital ministry in drawing it up](<https://lanation.bj/actualites/transformation-numerique-les-dsi-face-au-defi-de-lintelligence-artificielle>). In the last twelve months drafting began for a strategy that follows the [2021-2026 digital strategy, described by a GSMA study published in January 2025](<https://www.gsma.com/about-us/regions/sub-saharan-africa/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/BENIN_DigitalEconomy_Reflow_R2_Web.pdf>). No adopting act, public text, plan or reporting has been found for the 2031 strategy. Establishing would need the strategy adopted and its text public.

The [ministry's diagnostic report](<https://www.assises-resina.gov.bf/images/RAPPORT-DIAGNOSTIC_SUR_LA_Maturite_numerique_160421.pdf>) lists the strategy SN@DEN 2018-2027 as adopted on 6 June 2018. A [health ministry plan](<https://data.inafran.ru/files/Doc/Burkina%20Faso/Strategiceskij%20plan%20razvitia%20cifrovogo%20zdravoohranenia%20na%202025-2029%20gg.pdf>) of January 2025 lists it with the same period. On 25 August 2025 the government [presented a twelve-project roadmap to 2030](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/burkina-faso-outlines-12-digital-reforms-to-drive-transformation-by-2030>), and no adopting act has been found for it. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No published text of SN@DEN has been found. Establishing would need a public text of an adopted strategy whose period has not ended.

The government online coordinator said the SmartBots strategy was [adopted by cabinet in February 2020](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/62172>). The [ITU repository](<https://academy.itu.int/research-advocacy-and-convening-platforms/gcbi/repository-national-digital-skills-strategies>) gives its time frame as 2021-2026. In the last twelve months, on 23 September 2026, the President said the strategy and its action plan would be [formally launched in November 2026](<https://dailynews.gov.bw/news-detail/93397>). No published text of the strategy has been found, and no delivery plan or progress report has been found. Establishing would need a public text of the strategy, with its period not yet ended.

No stage is set. The Plan National Stratégique Centrafrique Digitale 2025 was last reported at a [workshop in November 2021](<https://oubanguimedias.com/2021/11/12/centrafrique-restitution-des-etudes-relatives-au-plan-national-strategique-centrafrique-digitale-2025-et-au-snid/>). Its period, 2020 to 2025, has ended. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No adoption or public text of the plan has been found, and no successor strategy has been found. Preparing would need a national digital strategy that is announced, being drafted or validated, or a successor in preparation now that the period has ended.

The ministry published the [strategy's own text](<https://www.telecom.gouv.ci/new/uploads/publications/171137227746.pdf>), version 1.4 of 26 January 2022, for the Stratégie nationale de développement du numérique 2021-2025. Its successor, the Stratégie nationale de transformation numérique 2025-2035, was [validated at a workshop on 19-22 August 2025](<https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099092225092021892/pdf/BOSIB-af66fe3f-3dfc-4703-ab9c-9f1fb5cf5714.pdf>). In the last twelve months, a workshop on 3 September 2026 [opened work toward 700 digital public services](<https://www.wearetech.africa/accueil/fils/actualites/gestion-publique/en-quete-d-efficacite-la-cote-d-ivoire-vise-700-services-publics-en-ligne-d-ici-2029>). No adopting act has been found for the successor, and no source found says its text is public. Establishing would need the successor adopted, with its text public.

The Plan stratégique Cameroun numérique 2020, dated May 2016, [calls itself the adopted strategic plan](<https://www.limko.cm/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/Plan-strategique-Cameroun-Numerique-2020-CM.pdf>) and names no adopting act. Its period ended by 2025. A [workshop on 3 July 2025](<https://patnuc.cm/2025/07/04/le-cameroun-trace-ses-sillons-dans-le-digital-avec-le-patnuc/>) discussed the diagnostic for updating it. In the last twelve months, in October 2026, the minister said [a draft national strategy for the digital economy was being finalised](<https://www.businessincameroon.com/public-management/2610-17054-cameroon-eyes-ai-led-growth-with-new-digital-economy-strategy>). No adopted text or period has been found for the new strategy. Establishing would need that strategy adopted, with a public text and a period that has not ended.

The [national validation workshop of 3-5 September 2019](<https://www.presidence.cd/uploads/files/Presentation%20PNN_03_final.pdf>) validated the Plan National du Numérique Horizon 2025, whose full text is on the Presidency's site. The ADN coordinator [said in November 2023 that it was adopted in 2019](<https://ouragan.cd/2023/11/digitalisation-de-la-rdc-ladn-et-lada-sengagent-a-former-100-000-agents>). In the last twelve months its successor, the Politique sectorielle de l'économie numérique 2026-2030, was [technically validated on 21-22 July 2026](<https://www.mediacongo.net/article-actualite-165910_economie_numerique_les_experts_valident_le_projet_de_politique_sectorielle_2026_2030.html>). No adopting act has been found for the plan or its successors. Establishing would need an adopted successor with a public text.

[Décret n° 2019-150 of 17 June 2019](<https://sgg.cg/JO/2019/congo-jo-2019-27.pdf>) approves Vision Congo Digital 2025, and it appeared in the Journal officiel of 4 July 2019. The ITU repository gives the [time frame as 2021 to 2025](<https://academy.itu.int/research-advocacy-and-convening-platforms/gcbi/repository-national-digital-skills-strategies>). A successor, Stratégie numérique 2030, was [reported complete on 13 October 2025](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/congo-nears-adoption-of-2030-digital-strategy>) and awaits approval by decree. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No public text of the strategy has been found, and no domestic budget line. Establishing would need a public text of an adopted strategy whose period has not ended.

The digital health strategy says the Government drew up Comores Numérique 2028 and [adopted it in 2018](<https://extranet.who.int/cpcd/sites/default/files/public_file_repository/com_comoros_strategie-nationale-de-sant-numerique_2022-2026.pdf>). Its [text is public on ANADEN's site](<https://anaden.org/uploads/media/5e3969272d9f8/strat-comores-numerique-v2-3-compresse.pdf>), and its roadmap runs from 2018 to 2028. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: on 25 August 2026 the minister said ANADEN is to [contribute to implementing the strategy across the economy](<https://alwatwan.net/societe/gouvernance-des-donn%C3%A9es-i-les-comores-se-dotent-d%E2%80%99une-strat%C3%A9gie-nationale.html>). No published report on results against the strategy's targets has been found. Operating would need such results published, and a domestic budget line.

[Resolução 72/2026](<https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/DownloadAct?id=101313>) lists the Estratégia para a Economia Digital de Cabo Verde as approved in September 2024, covering 2025 to 2030. On 25 November 2025 it was [presented to the Conselho Consultivo da Economia Digital](<https://www.governo.cv/a-economia-digital-e-um-pilar-estrategico-para-o-crescimento-de-cabo-verde-ministro-olavo-correia/>). In the last twelve months, a [consultation on 6 August 2026](<https://www.governo.cv/ministro-da-economia-comercio-industria-e-transicao-digital-promove-consulta-estrategica-sobre-o-futuro-digital-de-cabo-verde/>) covered the Agenda Digital de Cabo Verde 2035, which the resolution only [establishes the bases of](<https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/DownloadAct?id=101313>). No public text of the strategy has been found. Establishing would need that text to be public.

The [minister delegate for the digital economy presented the roadmap to the Council of Ministers in March 2023](<https://diplomatie.gouv.dj/Articles/DetailArticles/821>), as the Djibouti Smart Nation roadmap for the digital economy. The government record notes no adoption. The [Council of Ministers of 7 October 2025 listed drawing up a national digital strategy among the main challenges left](<https://www.presidence.dj/conseil-des-ministres/2025-10-07>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No adoption, text, period, delivery plan or report has been found for the roadmap. Establishing would need a national digital strategy adopted, with a public text and a period that has not ended.

On 12 May 2025 the High Commissioner called the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030 the [approved strategy](<https://www.echoroukonline.com/algeria-candidate-for-digital-leadership-in-africa-by-2030>). Its [text is published on the High Commission's site](<https://mail.webservices.dz/images/faq/hcn/SNTN-En.pdf>), in an August 2024 version. In the last twelve months, the [National Digital Services Centre was inaugurated on 5 July 2026](<https://www.jeune-independant.net/centre-national-des-services-numeriques-le-coeur-digital-de-letat-prend-vie/>), and on 12 July 2026 the Council of Ministers gave administrations [one month to connect to the National Data Center](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/algeria-sets-one-month-deadline-for-government-data-center-integration>). No adopting act, cost for the plan or domestic budget line has been found. Operating would need published results against the strategy's own targets.

The [ITU repository's 2025 listing](<https://academy.itu.int/research-advocacy-and-convening-platforms/gcbi/repository-national-digital-skills-strategies>) records the Digital Egypt Strategy as adopted, with a time frame of 2016 onward. On [13 March 2024](<https://cabinet.gov.eg/News/Details/75421>) the Prime Minister listed approval of a National strategy for building a fully digital state among the Supreme Council's objectives. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The latest figures found are from the [17 November 2024 briefing](<https://cabinet.gov.eg/News/Details/77765>). No adopting act, public text or domestic budget line has been found, and no approval of the fully digital state strategy. Establishing would need a public text of an adopted strategy.

[Levellers, in a legal-status page reviewed on 8 June 2026](<https://www.levellers.ai/what-is/ai-regulation-eritrea>), states that Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy. The page also says Eritrea has no published national AI strategy. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The only statement of absence is a third-party page, and no Eritrean government source has been found. No instrument in preparation has been found. Preparing would need a national digital strategy announced, being drafted, or validated and awaiting adoption.

The Council of Ministers [approved Digital Ethiopia 2030 on 29 November 2025](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_7816242>). The Prime Minister [launched it on 20 December 2025](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_7967007>) as the successor to Digital Ethiopia 2025, which covered 2020 to 2025. The Ministry of Innovation and Technology [describes the new strategy as a five-year journey to 2030](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_8021907>). In the last twelve months, on 30 July 2026, the National Digital Transformation Council [reviewed progress on the Digital Ethiopia Strategy, Fayda and 5 Million Coders](<https://www.fanamc.com/english/deputy-pm-says-technology-must-improve-lives-not-just-modernize-systems/>). No public text has been found for Digital Ethiopia 2030. Establishing would need that text to be public.

[On 3 April 2026 the minister presented the main orientations of the national digitalisation strategy to state IT directors](<https://www.gabonreview.com/transformation-numerique-de-letat-mark-alexandre-doumba-appelle-a-rompre-avec-les-initiatives-dispersees/>). [On 13 May 2026 the draft Stratégie nationale de Digitalisation et d'Innovation went to the technical committee](<https://agpgabon.ga/gabon-economie-numerique-tenue-de-la-3%e1%b5%89-reunion-du-cotech/>). [In June 2026 he outlined a digital development plan for 2025 to 2030](<https://itweb.africa/article/gabon-unveils-133m-digital-economy-drive/mYZRXM9gWpBvOgA8>). All three steps came in the last twelve months. The strategy is to follow the earlier Gabon Digital strategy, whose [time frame was 2020 to 2025](<https://academy.itu.int/research-advocacy-and-convening-platforms/gcbi/repository-national-digital-skills-strategies>). No adoption or public text has been found. Establishing would need the strategy adopted, with its text public.

The [Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation adopted the Digital Economy Policy in October 2024](<https://digitalpolicyalert.org/digest/dpa-digital-digest-ghana>). The [policy and strategy text is public](<https://moc.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Ghana-Digital-Economy-Policy-Strategy.pdf>), published in 2024. It [sets a target timeline of 2028 for its objectives](<https://moc.gov.gh/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Ghana-Digital-Economy-Policy-Strategy.pdf>) and lists actions with assigned responsibilities, but states no cost. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The ministry [began a successor strategy in April 2025](<https://www.gsma.com/about-us/regions/africa/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/GSMA_Ghana-Report_September-2025.pdf>), still in preparation. No progress report and no mandated body have been found. Operating would need published results against the policy's own targets, a mandated body and a domestic budget line.

[Version 1.2 of the strategy, dated 11 June 2024, calls itself the Transition Government's strategy](<https://ande.gov.gn/file/2025/01/Strategie-Numerique_Guinee-2027_v1.2.pdf>). [The full text is published as a PDF](<https://ande.gov.gn/file/2025/01/Strategie-Numerique_Guinee-2027_v1.2.pdf>), and [the strategy runs from 2023 to 2027](<https://ande.gov.gn/file/2025/01/Strategie-Numerique_Guinee-2027_v1.2.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 24 April 2026, [the digital economy ministry sought a consultant to draft a new ICT and digital economy policy](<https://224business.com/appels-offres/wardip-guinee-recrutement-dun-consultant-individuel-pour-la-revision-et-lactualisation-du-document-de-politique-et-strategie-nationales-des-tic-et-de-leconomie-numerique-pour-la/>) for 2026 to 2030. In December 2024 the minister had said the current strategy had been in implementation since 2022. No implementation or results report has been found, and no adopting act. Operating would need results published against the strategy's own targets.

The [National Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034 is issued by the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy](<https://mocde.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/National-Digital-Economy-Masterplan.pdf>). Its PDF is on the ministry's website, published in 2024. The [Digital Cooperation Organization reports that the government adopted the master plan](<https://dco.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Gambia-Report.pdf>). Its data is current to September 2024. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. An [article of 7 October 2026](<https://times.co.sz/45787/news/gender-checks-proposed-for-digital-policies/>) gives it as running 2024-2034. No delivery plan, reporting or adopting act has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against its targets.

[Decreto 10/2025 approves the ENTD.GW 2025-2030](<http://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/gbs235634.pdf>). The Council of Ministers approved it on 13 March, and the decree was published in the Boletim Oficial on 28 March 2025. The strategy's full text is [public as the annex to the gazetted decree](<http://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/gbs235634.pdf>), with 55 interventions that each have a start and end date. In the last twelve months, on 9 September 2026, [UNU-EGOV discussed a project document for carrying out the strategy with a ministry delegation](<https://unu.edu/egov/news/unu-egov-welcomes-delegation-guinea-bissau>). No published report against the strategy's targets has been found, and no cost for its actions. Operating would need published results against its own targets, and a mandated body.

[The Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Civil Aviation opened a World Bank-supported working week on 2 September 2026](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/el_ministerio_de_telecomunicaciones_acelera_la_transformacion_digital_con_el_respaldo_del_grupo_banco_mundial>) to complete and validate the Estrategia Nacional de Economía Digital. The ministry expected a consensus roadmap at its close. The earlier [ADIGE digital agenda was launched by the ministry in 2019 for 2019 to 2025](<https://www.guineaecuatorialpress.com/noticias/la_adige_esta_en_concordancia_con_la_uit_y_las_ods_de_la_onu>). The working week is the one step found in the last twelve months. No adopting act, period, plan, reporting or published text has been found for the strategy. Establishing would need the strategy adopted, with its text public.

[The Kenya National Digital Master Plan 2022-2032 is issued by the Ministry of ICT, Innovation and Youth Affairs](<https://cms.icta.go.ke/sites/default/files/2022-04/Kenya%20Digital%20Masterplan%202022-2032%20Online%20Version.pdf>). It was [unveiled and launched by ICT Cabinet Secretary Joe Mucheru on 12 April 2022](<https://www.kenyanews.go.ke/ten-year-national-digital-master-plan-unveiled/>). Its full text is published on the ICT Authority site. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed. [An ICT Authority tender of 15 September 2026 cites the plan's national target of 100,000 km of fibre network](<https://icta.go.ke/storage/tenders/mvLY8SauGos73NMInzM0Ox89ddABdCRrCR9WFSTJ.pdf>). No published report against the plan's targets has been found. No domestic budget line has been found. Operating would need results against the plan's own targets, published within three years.

[The strategy covers 2025 to 2029](<https://mopt.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Liberia-National-Digital-Strategy.pdf>), and its full text is on the ministry's website. It was [officially launched at the National Coordination Session of Digital Liberia Week, held during 28-30 October 2025](<https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/f00c8c982f5308548d0f81dd427e550c-0360012025/original/digital-liberia-event-book.pdf>). In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: the National Data Governance Policy of March 2026 [lists the National Digital Strategy (2025-2029) among the instruments Liberia has adopted](<https://mopt.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/2026-Liberia-Data-Governance-Policy-REVISED-CIPESA-1.pdf>). No progress report against the strategy's targets has been found, and no adopting act or date. Operating would need results published against its own targets.

[The Prime Minister approved the strategy on 21 April 2025](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2025/04/24/prime-minister-of-the-government-of-national-unity-approves-the-national-strategy-for-government-digital-transformation/>), following [the General Information Authority's December 2022 proposal](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/Libya-Digital-Transformation-Strategy-2023.pdf>). In the last twelve months, on 19 April 2026, the Authority [described Level 3 biometric digital identity trials as part of implementing the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2026/04/19/general-information-authority-central-bank-of-libya-national-authority-for-combating-money-laundering-with-the-relevant-authorities/>). [A National Committee for Digital Transformation is named responsible for it in November 2026](<https://alwasat.ly/news/485548>). Only the December 2022 proposal has been found as text, and no budget or results report. Establishing would need the approved text to be public.

[The finance minister told Parliament on 19 February 2025 that the Digital Transformation Strategy had been approved](<https://www.rsl.org.ls/sites/default/files/2025-02/Budget%20Speech%202025%2026%20Final%2019-02-2025.pdf>). The [strategy's text is published on the government's website](<https://www.gov.ls/download/lesotho-national-digital-transformation-strategy-2024-2030/>), self-dated 2024 and running to 2030. In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: [the 2027/28 Budget Strategy Paper of October 2026 commits government to fast-track the 2024-2030 strategy](<https://budgetportal.finance.gov.ls/PDFDocuments/2027-2028%20Budget%20Strategy%20Paper-639276738396119649.pdf>). No adopting act or date has been found, and no finance or results report. No detailed action plan has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and published results against the strategy's targets.

The [ITU repository](<https://academy.itu.int/research-advocacy-and-convening-platforms/gcbi/repository-national-digital-skills-strategies>) lists Digital Morocco 2030 among the strategies it says countries have adopted, with a time frame of 2024-2030. The [Government Council](<https://aujourdhui.ma/actualite/le-conseil-de-gouvernement-suit-une-presentation-sur-les-orientations-generales-du-developpement-numerique-maroc-digital-2030>) heard a presentation of its general orientations on 25 January 2024. In the last twelve months, the ministry [signed a memorandum with Capgemini Maroc](<https://www.wearetech.africa/fr/fils/actualites/tech/intelligence-artificielle-le-maroc-renforce-son-ecosysteme-avec-lappui-de-capgemini>) on AI skills on 17 July 2026 and [one with Orange Morocco](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/06/05/morocco-signs-ai-partnership-with-orange-morocco-to-advance-digital-transformation/>) on 4 June 2026. Both were presented as implementing Maroc Digital 2030. No public text has been found, and no adopting act or date is stated. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

Madagascar's digital ministry [estimates its budget at USD 800.169 million](<https://2424.mg/transformation-economique-letat-livre-un-plan-national-sur-le-numerique-dont-la-mise-en-oeuvre-coute-800-millions-de-dollars/>) for the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028. [Newsmada](<https://newsmada.com/2024/01/20/strategie-numerique-le-psn-accompagne-lemergence-dune-economie-numerique-a-madagascar/>) reports the digital minister presented the plan on 19 January 2024. In the last twelve months, the ministry and UNDP [handed over the final Digital Readiness Assessment report on 17 December 2025](<https://www.undp.org/fr/madagascar/communiques/remise-officielle-du-rapport-sur-levaluation-de-la-preparation-numerique-de-madagascar-dra>), which is to be the basis for a national roadmap. On 16 October 2026 [GSMA](<https://www.gsma.com/newsroom/press-release/gsma-digital-reforms-could-connect-1-12-million-more-people-in-madagascar-and-add-mga-4-1-trillion-to-gdp-by-2031/>) said its priorities support the plan. No source found says the plan was adopted or approved, and no public text has been found. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

Mali's Politique nationale de développement de l'économie numérique was [validated at a workshop on 24 October 2024](<https://www.maliweb.net/societe/avenir-numerique-du-mali-la-politique-nationale-de-developpement-de-leconomie-numerique-validee-3084246.html>). The [validated policy comes with an action plan for 2025-2029](<https://www.maliweb.net/societe/avenir-numerique-du-mali-la-politique-nationale-de-developpement-de-leconomie-numerique-validee-3084246.html>), while [Malijet](<https://malijet.com/education_et_formation_au_mali/305718-le-mali-lance-la-phase-iii-du-projet--les-filles-africaines-peuv.html>) describes the policy itself as covering 2021-2034. The minister is [quoted](<https://www.maliweb.net/societe/avenir-numerique-du-mali-la-politique-nationale-de-developpement-de-leconomie-numerique-validee-3084246.html>) giving an execution rate of 27.30% for the previous version, 2015-2020. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found states that the policy was adopted, and no public text has been found. Establishing would need a strategy that is adopted, has a public text and whose period has not ended.

The Council of Ministers [approved](<https://www.intic.gov.mz/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/BR_199_I_SERIE_2019.pdf>) the Plano Estratégico para a Sociedade de Informação 2019-2028 by Resolução n.º 52/2019, together with its Plano Operacional, on 26 February 2019. In the last twelve months, [Decreto n.º 4/2026](<https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/moz245120.pdf>) of 10 March 2026 tasked a new agency with mobilising resources for the Information Society Policy and its plans. [In May 2026 the draft digital transformation strategy went through regional validation](<https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Regional-Presence/Africa/Pages/projects/2026/mozambique-strategy.aspx>). The ITU says it covers 2027-2036 and awaits Council of Ministers approval. No source found gives actions or costs for the Plano Operacional, and no published report against the plan's targets has been found. Operating would need a delivery plan with dated actions or costs, and results published against the government's own targets.

The government [drew up and approved](<https://mtnima.gov.mr/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/La-Politique-Nationale-de-Participation-Electronique.pdf>) the Agenda national de transformation numérique 2022-2025 in 2022.
